court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
summary: Chief Justice's CourtSerial No.305-E HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD(LUCKNOW) *** [SECTION] ## Application under Section 378 No.37 of 2015 State of U.P. .....Appellant Through:- Mrs. Smiti Sahai, Additional Government Advocate v/s Rishiram .....Respondents [SECTION] ## CORAM : HON'BLE RAJESH BINDAL, CHIEF JUSTICE HON'BLE RAJEEV SINGH, JUDGE [SECTION] ## ORDER [SECTION] ## Rajeev Singh, J. 1.We have heard Mrs. Smiti Sahai, learned Additional GovernmentAdvocate for the State/appellant and have also.
judgmentText:
Chief Justice's CourtSerial No.305-E

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD(LUCKNOW)

***

[SECTION] ## Application under Section 378 No.37 of 2015

State of U.P.

.....Appellant

Through:- Mrs. Smiti Sahai, Additional Government Advocate

v/s

Rishiram

.....Respondents

[SECTION] ## CORAM : HON'BLE RAJESH BINDAL, CHIEF JUSTICE     HON'BLE RAJEEV SINGH, JUDGE

[SECTION] ## ORDER

[SECTION] ## Rajeev Singh, J.

1.We have heard  Mrs.  Smiti  Sahai, learned  Additional  GovernmentAdvocate for the State/appellant and have also perused the record availablebefore us.

2.By means of the present application under Section 378 (3) Cr.P.C., theState  has  sought  leave to  appeal  to  assail  the judgment  and  order  dated25.8.2014  passed  by  the  learned  Additional  Sessions  Judge,  Court  No.2,District  Hardoi,  whereby  the  learned  trial  court  has  acquitted  the

accused/respondent, namely, Rishiram, in the instant appeal for the offenceunder Sections 307 and 354 I.P.C, Police Station- Shahabad, District Hardoi.

3.Learned Additional Government Advocate has submitted that as per theprosecution  case,  on  15.12.2012  at  about  2:30  P.M.,  when  aunt  of  theinformant,  namely,  Sarojini  W/o  Basant  Lal  was  coming  to  her  home,respondent (Rishiram) with the intention to molest her, tried to drag her, thenshe raised objection, as a ressult, he had given number of blows with banka onher, in which, she received injuries on neck, face and right shoulder. On heralarm, informant-Krishna Kumar, daughter of Pooran Lal and other villagersreached on the spot and saved her. In the meantime, respondent fled away withthe banka.

4.Thereafter, the victim was brought to the police station in the injuredcondition and F.I.R. was lodged and victim was medically examined. Theaccused was arrested and on his pointing banka was recovered and recoverymemo was prepared, on the basis of all these facts and statement under Section161 Cr.P.C., charge-sheet was filed against the respondent under Section 307,354 I.P.C. Cognizance was taken by the learned court below and case wascommitted to the Court of Sessions. Charge was framed against the respondent,he pleaded not guilty and requested for trial.

5.The  prosecution  has  placed  7  witnesses  before  the  trial  court.Prosecution  also  relied  on  9  documentary  evidences  duly  proved  by  theaforesaid prosecution witnesses.

6.After completion of the prosecution evidences, statement under Section313 Cr.P.C. was recorded. Respondent denied the prosecution case.  Thereafter,the case was heard by the learned court below and after hearing the parties,respondent was acquitted.

7.Learned  Additional  Government  Advocate  has  submitted  that  thetestimony  of the injured  victim  was  ignored  by  the learned  court  below,wherein,  she  has  categorically  supported  the  prosecution  case,  therefore,learned court below has wrongly acquitted the respondents, therefore, kindindulgence of this Court is necessary and the application for leave to appeal isliable to be allowed by summoning the respondent.

8.Considering  the  arguments  of  the  learned  Additional  GovernmentAdvocate and going through the record, it is evident that the victim/injured hasstated that the respondent caused injuries on her neck, face and right shoulder 7.Learned  Additional  Government  Advocate  has  submitted  that  thetestimony  of the injured  victim  was  ignored  by  the learned  court  below,wherein,  she  has  categorically  supported  the  prosecution  case,  therefore,learned court below has wrongly acquitted the respondents, therefore, kindindulgence of this Court is necessary and the application for leave to appeal isliable to be allowed by summoning the respondent.

8.Considering  the  arguments  of  the  learned  Additional  GovernmentAdvocate and going through the record, it is evident that the victim/injured hasstated that the respondent caused injuries on her neck, face and right shoulder

and she also stated that she was brought to the Police Station by Basant Lal(husband), Bandhu Lal and Hariram by tractor and when they were going to thepolice station by tractor, Rishiram again attacked and he was caught by thepolice on the spot and brought to the Police Station by motor-cycle, it showsthat respondent was confined at the Police Station when F.I.R. was lodged butthe P.W.5, Sub Inspector, Rambabu (Investigating Officer) has deposed that hereceived information that respondent is sitting under a mango tree on the roadnear Malkapur with banka with intention to fleeing away, then police reachedthere and in the torch light, he was identified and caught at 7:10 P.M. It is alsoundisputed that case of the respondent was before the trial court that the victimwas having illicit relation with the respondent and she called him when herhusband was not at home but husband came there and due to annoyance, hecaused injuries to the victim (his wife) as well as respondent. As it is alsoevident that banka was not sent to F.S.L. for forensic examination, therefore,learned court below has rightly appreciated the evidences and acquitted therespondent by disbelieving the prosecution evidences.

9.As it is well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that while exercisingits appellate power, the High Court is empowered to re-appreciate, review andreconsider the evidence and this exercise is to be undertaken in order to cometo an independent conclusion and unless there are substantial and compellingreasons or very strong reasons to differ from the findings of the trial court, theHigh Court, as an appellate court in an appeal is not supposed to substitute itsfindings in case the findings recorded by the trial court are equally plausible.This view was taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramesh AndOthers vs. State of Haryana reported in (2017) 1 SCC 529 as well as AnwarAli and Another vs. State of Himachal Pradesh reported in (2020) 10 SCC166.

10.Thus, having considered the matter in its totality and in view of the lawlaid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in  Ramesh's case (supra) andAnwar Ali's  case (supra), we find  that  the learned  trial  court's  findingsregarding  acquittal  of  accused/respondents  herein  are  based  on  properappreciation and analysis of evidence available on record which do not in anymanner appear to be improbable or perverse.

11.On the basis of forgoing discussions, we are of the considered view thatthe application for leave to appeal lacks merit and deserves to be rejected andthe same is hereby rejected.

12.Since the application for leave to appeal has been rejected, the appealalso does not survive and the same stands dismissed.

(Rajeev Singh, J)          (Rajesh Bindal, C.J.)

Lucknow

court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
summary: Applicant :- Shamshuddin And OthersOpposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Anr.Counsel for Applicant :- Arvind Pratap SinghCounsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate,Girdhari Lal Shukla,Ram Kumar Srivastava [SECTION] ## Hon'ble Manish Kumar,J. Instant petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has beenpreferred by the petitioners for quashing of the summoningorder dated 23.11.2015 passed by Additional SessionsJudge, court no. 4, Gonda as well as entire proceedings ofcomplaint case no.10 of 2015 under.
judgmentText:
Applicant :- Shamshuddin And OthersOpposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Anr.Counsel for Applicant :- Arvind Pratap SinghCounsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate,Girdhari Lal Shukla,Ram Kumar Srivastava

[SECTION] ## Hon'ble Manish Kumar,J.

Instant  petition  under  Section  482  Cr.P.C.  has  beenpreferred by the petitioners for quashing of the summoningorder  dated  23.11.2015  passed  by  Additional  SessionsJudge, court no. 4, Gonda as well as entire proceedings ofcomplaint case no.10  of 2015 under Sections 323, 452,504, 506, 354-B and Section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that thepetitioners  have  falsely  been  implicated  in  the  presentcase and the complaint case filed by opposite party no. 2 isa narration of a forged and fabricated story. It is furthersubmitted that opposite party no. 2 is habitual to file suchcomplaints  once  in  a  year  either  against  one  of  thepetitioners  or  any  other  family  members.  It  is  furthersubmitted  that  a  civil  suit  has  been  preferred  by  thehusband of the complainant for permanent injunction inthe month of February, 2001.  It is further submitted thatthe  allegation  of  trying  to  outrage  the  modesty  or  anyoffence under Section 354-B of the IPC of the complainant'sminor  daughter  in  the  complaint  as  well  as  in  thestatement, is only against petitioner no. 3 and no suchallegation is against petitioner nos. 1 & 2 and hence, thepetitioner nos. 1 & 2 have illegally been summoned underSection 8 of the POCSO Act and Section 354-B of the IPC.

On  the  other  hand,  learned  AGA  and  Sri  Ram  KumarSrivastava,  learned  counsel  for  respondent  no.  2  havesubmitted  that  the  complainant  is  a  poor  lady  and  thepetitioners and his family members always used to harassthe  complainant  and  her  family  including  her  minordaughter for which complaints were made under Section156(3)  Cr.P.C.  on  10.07.2008,  20.08.2008,  04.02.2011,28.08.2012  and  an  FIR  dated  05.09.2015.  It  is  furthersubmitted that the husband of the complainant has alsofiled a regular suit no. 187/2001 for permanent injunctionagainst  Shamshuddin (petitioner  no.  1)  and  his  father-Islamuddin  and  other  family  members  but  unable  todispute the submissions raised by learned counsel for thepetitioners  that  the  allegation  of  trying  to  outrage  themodesty  of  the  complainant's  minor  daughter  and  thestatement  recorded  under  Section  200  Cr.P.C.  is  onlyagainst petitioner no. 3 and there is no such allegationagainst the petitioner nos. 1 & 2.

After  hearing  learned  counsel  for  the  parties  and goingthrough the record, it is found that the complaint is for twoincidents; first part is against the petitioner no. 3- Sikandar,who had tried to outrage the modesty of the complainant'sminor daughter and the second part is that the petitionersbarged in the house of opposite party no. 2 and startedassaulting the complainant and his family members andthreatened them on the gun point that if any case will belodged, the consequence will be faced by the complainantand even in  the  statement recorded  under  Section  200Cr.P.C.,  the  same  statement  has  been  given  as  it  isnarrated in the complaint case. The statement of the victimwas recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C., wherein she hasstated  almost  the  same  narration  as  stated  in  thecomplaint except one thing more has been added that shewas taken away by petitioner no. 3- Sikandar and Shadab(who is not the petitioner in the present petition) to theirhome and committed the offence, which falls under Section354-B  IPC.  The  said  allegation  is  not  made  against  thepetitioner nos. 1 & 2, as per the statement of the victimrecorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C. Under  these  circumstances  and  the  discussions  madehereinabove,  part  of  the  summoning  order  dated23.11.2015 by which the petitioner nos. 1 & 2 have beensummoned under Section 8 of the POCSO Act & Section354-B of the IPC  is  hereby quashed but for  rest of theSections  in  the  summoning  order  remain  intact.  So  farpetitioner no. 3 is concerned, there is no change in thesummoning order.

[SECTION] ## In view of above, petition is partly allowed.

At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioners submitsthat petitioners are ready to move bail application beforethe learned trial court which may be decided in view of thelaw  laid  by  Hon'ble  Supreme  Court  in  order  dated7.10.2021  passed  in  Petition  for  Special  Leave  toAppeal (Cri) No.5191 of 2021Satender Kumar Antilversus Central Bureau of Investigation and another.

Learned  AGA  has  no  objection  to  the  prayer  made  bylearned counsel for the petitioners.

On due consideration to the submissions of learned counselfor the parties', it is provided that in case, the petitionersappear before the trial court within fifteen days' from todayand file bail application, the same shall be decided within aperiod of ten days thereafter, in view of law laid down inthe  case  of  Satender  Kumar  Antil  versus  CentralBureau of Investigation and another (supra).

Applicant :- VijayOpposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.Counsel for Applicant :- Mahesh KumarCounsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Nirmal KumarPandey, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

Instant application has been filed with a prayer to release theapplicant on bail during the trial in Case Crime No. 474 of2020, under Section 3(1)of the U.P. Gangsters and Anti-SocialActivities (Prevention) Act, 1986 registered at Police StationRam Nagar, District Barabanki.

Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submits that theapplicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in theinstant matter. He added that there are six cases depicted in thegang chart against the applicant wherein he has been enlargedon bail. The bail orders have been annexed along with this bailapplication and the same has also been explained in para 7 ofthe bail application. Apart from the cases shown in the gangchart, there is no other previous criminal antecedent of theapplicant. He submits that he is a law abiding citizen and hewas never involved in committing the aforesaid offence. Hefurther submits that the applicant is not a member or leader ofany gang and he is languishing in jail since 29.10.2020. In case,the applicant is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty ofbail and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. for the State vehementlyopposed the contentions aforesaid but could not dispute the factthat the present applicant has been enlarged on bail six casesshown in the gang chart and further he could not dispute thefact regarding any other criminal history against the presentapplicant except the case depicted in the gang chart.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel of both sides,nature of accusation and severity of punishment in case ofconviction,  nature  of  supporting  evidence,  prima  faciesatisfaction of the Court in support of the charge, reformativetheory of punishment and without expressing any view on themerits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for bail.

Let the applicant- Vijay involved in the aforementioned crimebe released on bail, on his furnishing a personal bond and twosureties each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the courtconcerned, with the following conditions:-

(1)  The  applicant  shall  not  tamper  with  the  prosecutionevidence  by  intimidating/  pressurizing  the  witnesses,  orotherwise during the investigation or trial;

(2) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that heshall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidencewhen the witnesses are present in court. He shall remain presentbefore the trial court on each date fixed, either personally orthrough his counsel. In case of his absence, without sufficientcause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section229-A of the Indian Penal Code;

(3) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before thetrial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii)framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section313 Cr.P.C.; and

(4) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trialand in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before thecourt on the date fixed in such proclamation, the trial court shallinitiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law underSection 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will beverified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any ofthe above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty tocancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.

It is clarified that the observations made in this order are strictlyconfined to the disposal of this bail application and must not beconstrued to have any reflection on the merits of the case.

judgmentText:
Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. WRIT PETITION No. - 5510 of 2022

Petitioner :- Laxmi And Another

Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. And

Others

[SECTION] ## Counsel for Petitioner :- Punit Kumar ShuklaCounsel for Respondent :- G.A.

[SECTION] ## Hon'ble Ramesh Sinha,J.

[SECTION] ## Hon'ble Mrs. Saroj Yadav,J.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned A.G.A. forthe State-respondent.

This  petition  has  been  filed  for  a  writ  of  mandamuscommanding  the  respondents  not  to  create  unnecessaryhindrance in the peaceful marital life of the petitioners and notto disturb their mental peace and personal life and liberty.

It has been alleged that both the petitioners are major and havemarried with each other out of their own free will.  The age ofpetitioner no.1 is about 18 years as per her Transfer Certificate and  her  date  of  birth  is  01.07.2004  and  date  of  birth  ofpetitioner no.2 is 05.03.2000 as per his Aadhar Card. There isno first information report lodged against the petitioners tilldate.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the law laiddown in paragraph 17 of  Lata Singh Vs. State of U.P. andanother, 2006 (5) SCC 475 which reads as under:-

"17.....  We,  therefore,  direct  that  the  administration/policeauthorities throughout the country will see to it that if any boyor girl who is a major undergoes inter-caste or inter-religiousmarriage with a women or man who is a major, the couple isnot harassed by anyone nor subjected to threats or acts ofviolence, and anyone who gives such threats or harasses orcommits acts of violence either himself or at his instigation, istaken to task by instituting criminal proceedings by the police

against such persons and further stern action is taken againstsuch persons as provided by law."

The petitioners have also pleaded for protection under Article21 of the Constitution of India which guarantees liberty to leadlife of their own with dignity.

The petition is, therefore, disposed of with a direction to therespondents not to interfere in peaceful life and liberty of thepetitioners in any manner except in accordance with law.

It is made clear that if any F.I.R. is already registered on theissue, the order passed by this Court shall automatically standdischarged.

(Saroj Yadav, J.)     (Ramesh Sinha, J.) Order Date :- 4.8.2022

caseTitle: /688/2022 of Ashutosh @ Ashutosh Tiwari and Others Vs state of U.P. through Principal Secretary (Home Department ) lko and ors.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad

Through Principal Secretary (Home Department ) Lko And Ors.Counsel for Petitioner :- Ravindra Kumar SinghCounsel for Respondent :- G.A. Hon'ble Rakesh Srivastava,J.Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J. The First Information Report (FIR) dated 23.01.2022 registered as Case Crime No. 0021 of2022, under Sections 504, 506 IPC and 67 of the Information Technology Amendment Act,2008 at Police Station Talkatora, District Lucknow is.
judgmentText:
Petitioner :- Ashutosh @ Ashutosh Tiwari And OthersRespondent :- State Of U.P. Through Principal Secretary (Home Department ) Lko And Ors.Counsel for Petitioner :- Ravindra Kumar SinghCounsel for Respondent :- G.A.

Hon'ble Rakesh Srivastava,J.Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J.

The First Information Report (FIR) dated 23.01.2022 registered as Case Crime No. 0021 of2022, under Sections 504, 506 IPC and 67 of the Information Technology Amendment Act,2008 at Police Station Talkatora, District Lucknow is under challenge in the present writpetition. The Petitioners have also sought for stay of their arrest in the said case.

Heard Sri Ravindra Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the Petitioners and Sri S.N. Tilhari,learned Additional Government Advocate appearing on behalf of the State-Respondents.

We have gone through the First Information Report. The allegations made therein prima faciedisclose commission of a cognizable offence and as such, the same cannot be quashed. Thewrit petition lacks merit and is liable to be dismissed.

At this stage, learned counsel for the Petitioners has submitted that the offence allegedlycommitted entails a fine and a maximum imprisonment of seven years. As such, he prays thatinstead of arresting the Petitioners in a routine manner, the Investigating Officer be directed totake  recourse  to  the  procedure  provided  under  Section  41-A of  the  Code  of  CriminalProcedure 1973 ("Code").

Section  41  of  the  Code  deals  with  the  power  of  the  police  officer  investigating  thecommission of a cognizable offence, to arrest a person without an order from the Magistrateand without a warrant.

A perusal of Section 41 shows that there is no absolute bar against arresting a person accusedof an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years orwhich may extend up to seven years with or without fine. Section 41(1)(a), however, providesthat an investigating officer shall not arrest a person accused of such offences in a routinemanner and the arrest be made, only after following the restrictions imposed under Section41(1)(b).

In Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273, the Apex Court, while dealing with thepower of the police to arrest a person under Section 41 of the Code, has held that the saidpower is to be exercised only after the conditions enumerated in the said Section are satisfied.Paragraphs 7.1 and 7.2 of the said report being relevant are extracted below:

"7.1. From a plain reading of the aforesaid provision, it is evident that a personaccused of an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be lessthan seven years or which may extend to seven years with or without fine, cannotbe arrested by the police officer only on his satisfaction that such person hadcommitted the offence punishable as aforesaid. A police officer before arrest, insuch cases has to be further satisfied that such arrest is necessary to prevent suchperson from committing any further offence; or for proper investigation of thecase; or to prevent the accused from causing the evidence of the offence todisappear; or tampering with such evidence in any manner; or to prevent suchperson from making any inducement, threat or promise to a witness so as todissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or the police officer; or

unless such accused person is arrested, his presence in the court wheneverrequired cannot be ensured. These are the conclusions, which one may reachbased on facts.

7.2. The law mandates the police officer to state the facts and record the reasonsin writing which led him to come to a conclusion covered by any of the provisionsaforesaid, while making such arrest. The law further requires the police officers torecord the reasons in writing for not making the arrest. unless such accused person is arrested, his presence in the court wheneverrequired cannot be ensured. These are the conclusions, which one may reachbased on facts.

7.2. The law mandates the police officer to state the facts and record the reasonsin writing which led him to come to a conclusion covered by any of the provisionsaforesaid, while making such arrest. The law further requires the police officers torecord the reasons in writing for not making the arrest.

7.3. In pith and core, the police officer before arrest must put a question tohimself, why arrest? Is it really required? What purpose it will serve? What objectit will achieve? It is only after these questions are addressed and one or the otherconditions as enumerated above is satisfied, the power of arrest needs to beexercised.  In fine, before arrest first the police officers should have reason tobelieve on the basis of information and material that the accused has committedthe offence. Apart from this, the police officer has to be satisfied further that thearrest is necessary for one or the more purposes envisaged by sub-clauses (a) to(e) of clause (1) of Section 41 CrPC."

(emphasis supplied)

Thus, it is mandatory on the part of the investigating officer to record reasons for making anarrest as well as for not making an arrest in respect of a cognizable offence for which themaximum sentence is up to seven years.

Where, however, arrest is not required to be made under Sub-Clause (1) of the amendedSection 41 of the Code, the police is bound to issue a notice of appearance to the accusedperson. Even in such a case, failure to comply with the notice of appearance or unwillingnessto identify himself may be grounds for the police to arrest a person to whom a notice underSection 41-A of the Code has been issued.

Learned  Additional  Government  Advocate,  on  the  basis  of  instructions,  states  that  theprovisions of Section 41 and 41-A of the Code would be scrupulously complied with by theinvestigating officer.

The statutory protection under Section 41 and 41-A of the Code is already available, whichthe police authorities are bound to comply in this case also.

With the aforesaid observation, the Writ Petition stands disposed of.

Order Date :- 15.2.2022Pradeep/-

(Saurabh Lavania, J.)    (Rakesh Srivastava, J.)
